newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia tells regions to pay up or have budgets cut.
newsitem.headline: Russia tells regions to pay up or have budgets cut.

text.p: Russia will cut allocations to regions which refuse to take part in a new bond issue programme to recover $1.6 billion in unrepaid Treasury credits, Deputy Finance Vasilya Kovalyov said late on Thursday.
"Over each of three months, 33 percent of the credit amount will be deducted from federal support to the region," Kovalyov told a news conference.
The federal government has set up a programme to allow regions to issue bonds to pay nine trillion roubles ($1.6 billion) in defaulted 1996 agricultural credits owed to the federal government.

The first auction of discount bonds with 10 percent coupons and one, two and three-year maturities was last week and attracted the attention of foreign investors looking for higher-yielding Russian paper than Treasury Bills.
But Kovalyov said 10 of 77 regions which had not paid back seed, gasoline and other credits extended last spring, to be repaid after the 1996 harvest, had refused to address the issue.
"Not all regions treated the problem positively," he told a news conference. "These regions will not only suffer financial, but moral damage by pushing their investment ratings lower."

Many Russian regions, including Irkutsk, Nizhny Novgorod and Perm, which refused to issue the bonds in the federal programme and owe for the agricultural credits, are planning Eurobonds to raise funds cheaply abroad.
"I can warn them that the information that a region is not paying its debts cuts its investment rating sharply," Kovalyov said. "Nothing happens unnoticed on the financial markets.
"By October 1 the 1996 credit saga must be over," he said, adding that after the first auction the volume of debt had fallen to 7.7 trillion roubles from nine trillion.
